subject: Re: Hosted API — data disposition, TTLs, and deletion attestation
messages:
From: Maya Rodriguez <maya@novasystems.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alan Cheng <alan.cheng@novasystems.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2029 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API — residency/retention/deletion details for EU deployment

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. Procurement and security here at Nova Systems asked for a short written summary to feed into our RFP and DSAR playbook. Could you confirm the following for the Redwood hosted API when the tenant is configured for EU-only region storage?

1) Where is customer request content (prompts + responses) stored at rest? Which physical regions and cloud providers?
2) Standard retention windows for: API logs, request/response payloads, KV/prefix caches, analytics/metrics, and backups/snapshots.
3) Timeline and process for a verified deletion request (customer-initiated erasure): immediate removal from active stores vs backups, and attestation / proof artifact timing.
4) Do you ever use customer request/response data to train models or for product analytics beyond aggregated metrics?

If you can include any constraints (e.g., regulatory hold exceptions) and an indicative SLA for deletion attestation, that would help. We may test erasure during POC.

Appreciate a concise answer we can share with compliance.

Best,
Maya
Maya Rodriguez
Senior Security Program Manager — Nova Systems

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rodriguez <maya@novasystems.com>
Cc: Alan Cheng <alan.cheng@novasystems.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2029 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API — residency/retention/deletion details for EU deployment

Hi Maya — thanks, and great questions. Below is a concise, operational summary we provide customers for EU-hosted tenants. Happy to run through this on a quick screenshare and walk through an erasure test during your POC.

1) Storage locations and providers:
- Customer request/response content (raw prompts & generated tokens) is stored only in the region you select when provisioning the tenant. For EU tenants we persist in AWS eu-west-1 by default; GCP europe-west6 possible on request for enterprise customers.
- Metadata required for routing (tenant id, geo-flag) is stored in our control plane. For EU-locked customers we offer an EU-only control plane option; otherwise control-plane metadata may be stored in the US.

2) Retention windows (default hosted API offering):
- Active request/response payloads: retained in primary store for up to 30 days by default, configurable down to 0 days for customers with stricter needs.
- KV/prefix caches (inference cache, ephemeral KV): cleared on erase request; typical TTLs are 24–72 hours depending on workload. We proactively evict caches within 48 hours after a verified erasure.
- API/server logs (request metadata, latency, error traces): retained 90 days in readable form; aggregated anonymous metrics retained 12 months.
- Backups & snapshots: incremental backups are kept for replay/recovery and are automatically rotated. By default snapshots are retained for up to 120 days; backups are eligible for secure overwrite during the 120–150 day window. For enterprise EU-tenants we can shorten this to 30/60/90-day retention on contract.
- Audit & billing records (transactional): retained 365 days for billing reconciliation by default; can be scoped by agreement.

3) Deletion (erasure) process and timeline:
- Verification: customer initiates via the Console or a signed DSAR request. We verify requestor identity per DPA/contract.
- Active stores: within 24 hours of a verified request we mark and remove customer payloads from primary stores and disable any active caches.
- Cache eviction: in 48 hours we propagate cache clears to all serving nodes for that tenant.
- Logs & analytics: logs containing PII are redacted/pseudonymized within 72 hours where feasible; full purging from log systems occurs on the next scheduled log rotation subject to the 90-day window described above unless a shorter contractual window is in effect.
- Backups & snapshots: we schedule deletion/overwrite during the next backup cycle; in standard hosting this completes within up to 120 days. For customers requiring quicker eradication we offer a certified one-time backup purge for an additional fee and process (typical completion 7–30 days depending on storage provider constraints).
- Attestation: after completion we provide a signed deletion certificate (timestamped manifest of affected objects + storage locations) within 7 business days for standard erasures, or within 3 business days if on the enterprise expedited path.

Exceptions: legal holds (court orders, regulatory holds) will prevent immediate erasure and are surfaced to the customer with the specific scope and timeline.

4) Use for model training / analytics:
- By default we do not use customer request/response content to train public models.
- Aggregated, non-identifying telemetry (usage counts, latency distributions, model performance metrics) may be used internally to improve system reliability and model routing decisions.
- Customers can opt into a research/training program under a separate opt-in agreement.

Next steps: if Nova wants to run a live erasure test during POC we can schedule a controlled test and deliver the attestation artifacts. I’m attaching our residency SLA excerpt and our deletion playbook for reference (attached).

Thanks — will loop laura for the attestation packaging and priyom for any contract tweaks.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Thanks Sean — this is helpful. Quick clarifications before I share with our legal team:

- You said "we do not use customer request/response content to train public models" — can you confirm whether any internal feature engineering or debugging traces might capture example prompts (even transiently) and whether those ever leave the tenant region?
- For the backup purge option (7–30 days): what evidence do you provide that a snapshot containing the erased data has been overwritten (audit log or storage provider confirmation)?

If you can add a single-line response to each point that I can paste into our questionnaire that would be ideal.

Appreciate it,
Maya

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 5 Jun 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API — residency/retention/deletion details for EU deployment

Hi Maya — quick single-line answers below, suitable for inclusion in a questionnaire. Looping in Laura and Priyom to prepare the formal artifacts and the attestation pack.

- Internal debugging/feature traces: "Transient debugging traces may capture snippets of requests for per-request troubleshooting but are stored only in the tenant's region and are excluded from model-training pipelines; customers can request redaction or deletion as part of a DSAR."

- Backup purge evidence: "For the expedited backup purge we provide a signed manifest and storage-provider delete/overwrite confirmation where available plus an internal audit record showing the purge job execution; when provider confirmations are not issued we provide the job execution logs and object manifests with timestamps."

We'll follow up with the signed deletion certificate and the residency SLA pdf.

Best,
Sean

P.S. Internal note: Laura/Priyom — please prepare the attestation package (residency-sla-20290604.pdf, deletion-playbook-REDWOOD.md) and confirm whether the EU control plane option can be toggled for the POC tenant. I will propose the erasure test slot for next Wednesday.
